subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Neptune's Other Moons
description: Learn Neptune's Other Moons in one minute.

hook.text: Neptune has 16 known moons, but Triton dominates. The rest are tiny, dark, and largely mysterious.

buildup.text: Nereid has one of the most eccentric orbits of any moon—swinging from close to Neptune out to enormous distances.

discovery.text: Hippocamp, discovered in 2013, is just 34 km across. It may be a fragment blasted off the larger moon Proteus by an impact.

twist.text: Triton's capture likely destroyed or ejected Neptune's original moons. The current small moons formed from the debris afterward.

climax.text: Only Voyager 2 has visited Neptune. Most moons were discovered by Earth telescopes and Hubble after the flyby.

punchline.text: Tiny survivors of Triton's capture. A system reshaped by one dramatic arrival.

quiz.question: How did Triton's capture affect Neptune's original moon system?
options: It likely destroyed or ejected the original moons, and current small moons formed from debris
It had no effect—Neptune's moons were already in their current orbits
Triton absorbed all the original moons during its capture

details.summary: Besides Triton, Neptune has 15 other known moons — all small and irregular. Most are captured objects in distant, eccentric orbits. The innermost small moons orbit within or near Neptune's ring system.
details.whyItMatters: Neptune's small moons illustrate how gravitational capture, collisions, and ring-moon interactions shape satellite systems. They show that even in the distant outer solar system, moon formation is a violent, ongoing process.
takeaways: 15 other known moons besides Triton, all small
Most are captured objects in irregular orbits
Hippocamp may be a fragment from a collision with Proteus

faq.question: Did Triton's capture destroy Neptune's original moons?
faq.answer: Likely yes. When Triton was captured into its initially eccentric orbit, it would have gravitationally scattered or destabilized any pre-existing regular moon system. The current inner moons may have re-accreted from the debris after Triton's orbit circularized.

faq.question: How was Hippocamp discovered so recently?
faq.answer: Hippocamp is tiny (34 km) and was hidden in Neptune's glare. Mark Showalter discovered it in 2013 by stacking Hubble images and processing them to remove Neptune's light. Its orbit near the much larger Proteus, combined with its composition, suggests it's a fragment from a past impact on Proteus.
